skill.name: generative-art
skill.description: Create algorithmic generative art with p5.js, seeded randomness, interactive controls, and browser-ready HTML artifacts.
skill.summary: Creates seeded p5.js generative art with interactive controls and reproducible variations.
skill.author: Cam10001110101

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline file references, CSS borders, comments, and JavaScript RegExp.exec. The confirmed findings are low-severity remote resource dependencies for p5.js and Google Fonts, which should be documented or self-hosted for stricter environments. No prompt injection or malicious intent was found in the reviewed files.

remediation.issue: Generated artifacts load p5.js from cdnjs.
remediation.suggestion: Keep the version pinned and document the network dependency, or self-host p5.js for offline or locked-down use.

remediation.issue: Viewer template loads Google Fonts from external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Offer local font fallbacks or self-host fonts when artifacts must avoid third-party requests.

content.value_statement: Artists and teams need reproducible generative art that can be explored without setup. This skill turns a concept into a seeded p5.js HTML artifact with controls and PNG export.
actual_capabilities: Creates a short algorithmic philosophy before implementation.
Builds a single self-contained HTML artifact for browser or Claude artifact use.
Uses p5.js with seeded randomness for reproducible variations.
Adds seed navigation, parameter controls, reset, regenerate, and PNG download actions.
Provides reference templates for p5.js structure and viewer layout.
limitations: Generated artifacts load p5.js and fonts from external CDNs unless modified.
It does not produce finished bitmap images directly.
Output quality depends on the model implementing the algorithm.
Complex sketches may need performance tuning for mobile devices.

use_cases.title: Prototype generative visuals
use_cases.description: Digital artists can turn a theme into a seed-based p5.js sketch with adjustable controls.

use_cases.title: Explore campaign artwork
use_cases.description: Design teams can generate browser-ready visual studies for posters, headers, or social assets.

use_cases.title: Teach algorithmic art
use_cases.description: Educators can demonstrate noise, particles, recursion, and deterministic randomness through interactive examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a first sketch
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple themed artwork.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an interactive generative art artifact inspired by ocean currents. Include a short algorithmic philosophy and simple seed controls.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a visual direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a p5.js generative art artifact based on quiet city lights. Make three adjustable parameters and keep the output reproducible.

prompt_templates.title: Design campaign art
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for applied brand visuals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an algorithmic art system for a product launch background. Use seeded randomness, tuned controls, and a PNG download action.

prompt_templates.title: Build a custom system
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request that expects a detailed computational concept.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced generative artwork from this concept: [concept]. Explain the computational philosophy, define custom parameters, and produce a self-contained HTML artifact.

output_examples.input: Create generative art inspired by migrating constellations.
output_examples.output: An algorithmic philosophy about orbital migration, plus an interactive seeded artwork with constellation density and motion controls.

output_examples.input: Make a browser artifact for abstract botanical growth.
output_examples.output: A self-contained p5.js viewer with seed navigation, branch growth controls, color pickers, reset, regenerate, and PNG download.

output_examples.input: Create 20 reproducible variations for a poster study.
output_examples.output: A seed-driven art system where each seed creates a consistent variation that can be reviewed and exported from the viewer.

best_practices: Start with a clear concept that can become motion, structure, or field behavior.
Keep parameter ranges small enough for responsive previews.
Review external resource use before sharing generated HTML artifacts.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a static image when you need an editable algorithm.
Do not remove seed controls if reproducible variations matter.
Do not rely on very high particle counts without testing performance.

faq.question: Does this skill create images directly?
faq.answer: No. It creates interactive HTML artifacts that can export PNG images from the canvas.

faq.question: Can the same seed reproduce the same artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill instructs the generated p5.js sketch to use seeded randomness.

faq.question: Does the artifact need a server?
faq.answer: No. The generated HTML is designed to open directly in a browser or Claude artifact.

faq.question: Can users adjust the artwork?
faq.answer: Yes. The template includes sliders, seed navigation, color controls, and action buttons.

faq.question: Are there external network requests?
faq.answer: Yes. The template loads p5.js and fonts from public CDNs unless the generated artifact is modified.

faq.question: Is this useful for production artwork?
faq.answer: It is best for prototypes and studies. Final production use should include review, testing, and asset hosting decisions.
